privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Shelfmark is a personal project that stores the links you save. This page explains what we keep and why, in plain words.

store.title: What we store
store.account: From Google or GitHub: your name, email address and avatar (a link to your profile picture). They are used to sign you in and to show who is signed in. Your account record also holds which provider you used and your id there.
store.content: Your links (address, title, note, favorite mark, when you last opened it), your folders and your tags.
store.images: For each link, a small copy of the site's icon and preview image, if the site has them. Our server downloads and stores them so they load from Shelfmark.
store.feedback: Your answers to the in-app rating, linked to your account: a score from 1 to 10 and, if you write one, a comment.
store.promptViews: The app also counts how often the rating prompt was shown to you and when, to know which prompts get answered. These counts belong to your account and are deleted with it.
store.stats: The "Your shelf" numbers on the Account page (counts, the sites and tags you use most, links per week) are worked out from your own data each time you open the page. They are not stored and never shared.
store.usage: To learn how Shelfmark is used, we record the day you last used the app: a date only, no time, page or action. The author sees only totals worked out from all accounts together, such as how many people use folders or tags or which themes are popular. Groups of fewer than three people are not shown, and no one's links, notes or settings are looked at one by one. These totals are worked out on request and are not stored. When you delete your account, the date goes with it.
store.sessions: For each sign-in: when it expires, plus the IP address and the browser (user agent) it was started from, to keep sessions secure.
store.logs: Our API logs the request method, path, status, duration and a request id, without link contents or personal data. Our host, Vercel, keeps its own standard request logs, which include IP addresses, for a limited time.

cookies.title: Cookies and browser storage
cookies.necessary: We use strictly necessary cookies only. A session cookie keeps you signed in, in the demo as well. A short-lived cookie protects the Google and GitHub sign-in flow. They are httpOnly and SameSite=Lax, and Secure on the live site. Signing out removes the session cookie.
cookies.none: There are no advertising, analytics or tracking cookies, and no analytics scripts.
cookies.storage: Your browser's local storage holds interface preferences only: the theme, the language and the cards or list view. They stay in your browser. The installed app (PWA) caches Shelfmark's own files for fast start-up, not your links.

dont.title: What we don't do
dont.sell: We don't sell or share your data and don't show ads.
dont.read: We don't use the content of your links for statistics: only counts (links, folders, ratings), never addresses or titles. Your links are stored in our database so the app can show, search and preview them; only the author of the service has access to it.
dont.training: We don't use your links, notes or summaries to train AI models, and we don't let our AI provider do so.

previews.title: Link previews
previews.body: When you save a link, our server visits that page to read its title, icon and preview image. The site therefore sees our server's IP address and the user agent "ShelfmarkBot", not your IP address.

extension.title: Browser extension
extension.body: The Shelfmark extension for Chrome, Edge, Brave and Arc works only when you click its button, press its shortcut or choose “Save link to Shelfmark” or “Save page to Shelfmark” in the right-click menu, never in the background. It then sends Shelfmark the address of that one tab, to check whether you saved it already, and saves its address and title, with the folder, tags and note you pick, only when you press Save. It never sees your history or the other sites you visit. If you click “Fill in with AI” and AI is on in your account, it also sends Shelfmark that address and title, and your note when AI may read notes, to get AI suggestions, handled under the same AI terms as in the app. If you switch to “All tabs”, your browser asks once for the optional tabs permission; switching then checks the addresses of your open tabs (without any #fragment) against your library, to mark the ones you saved already. Nothing is saved until you press Save, and only the tabs you tick are saved or sent for AI suggestions. From the right-click menu it sends Shelfmark the address of the link or page you chose (and the page’s title), checks whether you saved it already and, if not, saves it at once to the folder your rules pick, or to Unsorted.
extension.access: It uses your Shelfmark sign-in in that browser and cannot read the sign-in cookie itself. It can reach Shelfmark only, and keeps just the folders you saved to most recently on your device, to offer them next time.

third.title: Other services
third.signin: Sign-in goes through Google or GitHub. They receive the fact that you sign in to Shelfmark, and each has its own privacy policy:
third.tokens: We do not store the access tokens that Google or GitHub issue when you sign in.
third.avatar: Your profile photo is loaded directly from Google or GitHub, so your browser contacts them whenever Shelfmark shows it. No referrer is sent with that request, so they don't see which Shelfmark page you are on.
third.monitoring: If error monitoring is switched on, crashes and server errors are reported to Sentry through our own server. Reports are scrubbed before they leave: no email, IP address, cookies, request contents or saved link addresses, only technical details such as the error type, where in the code it happened, your browser and system type, the page path and a request id. If it is off, nothing is sent.

where.title: Where it lives
where.hosting: The API runs on Vercel in the fra1 region (Frankfurt) and the database on Neon in eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). The app's static files are served from Vercel's global network.

ai.title: AI features (optional)
ai.intro: AI is off until you turn it on in Settings › AI. When it is on, it suggests tags and folders and writes short summaries. Everything it makes is marked with a small spark and may be inaccurate; nothing is applied unless you accept it or choose automatic mode.

processor.text: Anthropic PBC (USA), as our processor, only to produce the result you asked for.

sent.text: a link's address, title, description and text extracted from the page, and the names of your tags and folders. Your notes only if you turn on "Include my notes". Never your other links, your account details or anyone else's data.

kept.text: Anthropic deletes the request within 30 days and doesn't use it for training; only content its safety systems flag may be kept longer (up to 2 years), or where the law requires it. The results (tags, summaries) are stored with your links and deleted with them.

counted.text: only the number of AI requests per account, for your monthly limit. As everywhere in Shelfmark, statistics use counts only, never what you saved.

off.text: switch off one feature or AI as a whole in Settings › AI; requests stop at once. "Delete AI data" there removes every summary and suggestion AI made.

meaning.text: while it is on (Settings › AI), the title, summary and tag names of each link, your note only with "Include my notes", and the words you search for are sent to Voyage AI, our second processor, which turns them into number vectors. Never the address, your folders or anyone else's data. The vectors are stored with your links and deleted with them or with "Delete AI data"; your search text is not stored. Voyage AI by MongoDB (USA) deletes each request right after processing it (zero-day retention) and doesn't use it for training.

ask.text: only when you ask a question, your question, the earlier questions and answers of the open chat and the links of yours that the assistant looks up with read-only search, count and list tools (title, address without its query, folder and tag names, summary, your note only with "Include my notes") are sent to [PROVIDER]. The answer cites and shows only your own links. While "Keep Ask history" is on (the default), each finished question and answer is stored with your account so you can open the conversation again: the links only as references to your own links (never copies), at most 50 conversations, each deleted 30 days after its last question. You can delete one conversation or all of them, turn the history off in Settings › AI, and "Delete AI data" and deleting your account remove it; the data export includes it. Off, nothing is stored. We also count the number of questions per day and month (and how many got a deeper answer), for your limit.

retention.title: How long we keep it
retention.data: We keep your account and everything in it until you delete it.
retention.sessions: A sign-in lasts 7 days and is extended when you use the app, at most once a day. After that you sign in again.
retention.demo: The demo is a temporary sandbox with sample links. It ends after 24 hours, and a daily cleanup job deletes expired demo accounts with all their data. To limit abuse we keep a one-way hash of the network address that opened the demo, never the address itself, and it is deleted with the demo account.

control.title: Your control
control.export: In Settings you can export your links, folders, tags and notes as JSON or as a browser bookmarks file (HTML).
control.delete: You can delete any link at any time, or delete your whole account in Settings. Your account is then kept for 7 days in case you change your mind, after which it and all its data are removed from the database. Backups kept by the database provider may take a short while to expire.

security.title: Security
security.body: Data is sent over HTTPS. Each account can only reach its own data. Sign-in uses Google or GitHub, so we never see or store a password.

children.title: Children
children.body: Shelfmark is not directed at children, and we do not knowingly collect data from them.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.body: If the way Shelfmark handles data changes, we update this page and its "Last updated" date.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: For questions about this policy or your data, open an issue in the GitHub repository.
contact.noPersonal: Issues are public, so please do not put personal data in them.

motionBatch.text: Livelier motion: a dragged link sways and flies into its folder, the highlight glides between rows, checks draw themselves and changed numbers roll.

extensionTabs.text: The browser extension saves several open tabs at once, with one folder and tags for all (version 1.2.0, rolling out in the Chrome Web Store).

folderStyle.text: Give a folder a color, an icon or emoji, a description and a cover, and highlight it with a background in the sidebar.

domainRules.title: Rules by site
domainRules.text: Send links from a site straight to the folder you choose.
domainRules.alt: A rule that sends links from one site to a folder.

reminders.title: Reminders
reminders.text: Ask Shelfmark to remind you about a link later.
reminders.alt: A saved link with a reminder.

colourPicker.text: Own colors: the + button is centered, and a picked color applies right away in a readable shade.

phoneSignIn.text: Small cards fly onto the shelf while you sign in on a phone.

appSkeleton.text: After you sign in, the app takes shape at once instead of showing a black screen.

ukrainian.text: Shelfmark now speaks Ukrainian. Choose it in Settings › Language.

noHttps.text: A link typed as example.com saves like any other.

refresh.title: A fresh look
refresh.text: Softer corners, calmer colors, a floating tab bar on phones and toasts that say what happened.

trash.title: Trash
trash.text: Deleted links and folders wait in Trash, so nothing is gone by accident. You choose how long they stay.

folders.title: Folder colors, icons and pins
folders.text: Give a folder a color and an icon or emoji, and pin the ones you use most to the sidebar.

savedViews.title: Saved views
savedViews.text: Keep a filter you use often, like videos or articles to read, one click away.

sharing.title: Share a folder
sharing.text: Turn a folder into a public page anyone with the link can open. Stop sharing at any time.

pasteMany.title: Paste many links
pasteMany.text: Paste a whole list of links and save them in one go.

bulk.title: Select several links
bulk.text: Move, tag, favorite or delete many links at once.

dragDrop.title: Drag and drop
dragDrop.text: Drag a link onto a folder in the sidebar, or reorder your folders.

theme.title: Your own theme
theme.text: Choose your own accent, background and corners, and how much the app animates.

languages.title: Six languages
languages.text: Use Shelfmark in English, French, German, Italian, Spanish or Portuguese.

feedback.title: Send feedback
feedback.text: Tell us what works and what doesn't, with a screenshot if you like, right from the app.

fastLanding.text: On a first visit the landing opens at once instead of after a dark pause.

phoneKeyboard.text: On phones the keyboard no longer covers the folder list, sheets, dialogs and suggestions.

emptyExport.text: Export explains when there is nothing to export instead of downloading an empty file.

bulkBar.text: On phones the bar for selected links sits just above the tab bar again.

sheetDropdown.text: A dropdown closes as soon as you drag a sheet down on a phone.

skeletonRows.text: The loading screen matches the page and shows three rows of cards.

feedbackActive.text: Send feedback no longer stays highlighted after you close it.

folderChips.text: Cards and rows show which folder a link is in, in the folder's color.

updatePrompt.text: When a new version is ready, Shelfmark asks before reloading.

whatsNewCard.text: A What's new card after each update, and a page that lists every release.

privacyWording.text: The privacy page says more clearly what is stored and who can see it.

toastWraps.text: Notifications show their whole text instead of cutting it off.

folderStyleRace.text: Changing a folder's style quickly no longer brings back an older choice.

newFolderInAddLink.text: Add link can create a folder: type a new name in the Folder field.

emojiPickerTabs.text: The emoji picker is as wide as its field, and its category tabs no longer look like emoji to pick.

aiSuggestions.title: Fill in with AI
aiSuggestions.text: One click in Add link fills in the title, folder, tags and a short summary from the page. Change anything you like: your choice always wins. Works in the browser extension too. AI stays off until you turn it on in Settings › AI.
aiSuggestions.alt: The Add link dialog with a YouTube address, filled in by AI: title, folder, tags and a summary.

aiSummaries.title: Short summaries
aiSummaries.text: With AI on, links get a one- or two-line summary on their card. Edit it and it's yours.
aiSummaries.alt: Link cards with a short AI summary under each title.

aiTidy.title: Tidy Unsorted with AI
aiTidy.text: Review the AI suggestions for everything in Unsorted on one page and apply them with one Undo. File a site's links into the same folder a few times and Shelfmark offers a rule.

aiAsk.title: Ask your shelf
aiAsk.text: Ask a question in your own words and get a short answer from the links you saved, with every source listed. Open it with Ask next to search, or the Ask tab on your phone.
aiAsk.alt: The Ask drawer with a question, a short answer and the links it comes from.

aiCleanup.title: Library clean-up
aiCleanup.text: Find links you saved more than once and tags that mean the same, review every change and apply them in one step, with one Undo. Copies go to Trash.

mcp.title: Connect your assistant
mcp.text: On Pro, Claude and other MCP assistants can search and read your links with a personal token. Read-only, and you can revoke it any time.

aiSearch.title: Search by meaning
aiSearch.text: Search finds links that match what you mean, not only your words, and says why each one matched. Edit link shows related links from your shelf, and Side by side can offer their folders.
aiSearch.alt: Search results with a Related by meaning group below the word matches.

extensionInStore.text: The Shelfmark browser extension is in the Chrome Web Store: install it from the banner on your shelf or from Settings › Library.

forgotten.title: Forgotten links
forgotten.text: Links you saved and never opened wait in Recently opened › Forgotten. The count shows next to Recently opened.

cardTags.text: Link cards show whole tags and a “+N” for the rest instead of cutting a tag off.

phoneFolders.text: On phones the Library lists Folders right under Pinned.

dialogButtons.text: In dialogs on phones the main action sits alone at the bottom.

textFields.text: Text fields grow with what you type.

landingHeadline.text: The landing page headline fits every language.

askAnswers.text: Ask your shelf answers questions again.

youtubeTitles.text: YouTube links get their video title and author.

clearedSummary.text: A summary you cleared in Add link stays empty after saving.

cardTagsWhole.text: Tags on cards are never cut off: the first tag, then “+N” with all tags on hover.

bulkBarFits.text: The selection bar shows every button on narrower windows.

aiDialogIcon.text: The AI announcement shows its icon at once, without a scrollbar.

searchChoice.text: Choosing a search result no longer freezes the app.

backfillProgress.text: “Process existing links” moves on while the app is open.

aiNewTags.text: AI fills in one or two new tags and suggests more.

askChat.title: Ask your shelf is now a chat
askChat.text: Ask follow-up questions, ask how many links you have on a topic, and get the links it finds as cards you can open at once. Drag the edge of the panel to make it wider.
askChat.alt: The Ask your shelf panel answering “Find my design links” with five links shown as cards.

toastsSmooth.text: Several notifications open up and fold back smoothly when you point at them.

cardTagsFit.text: A tag on a card is shown whole or moves into “+N”, which lists only the tags not on the card.

focusRingAfterKey.text: Opening a dialog with a click or tap no longer shows a focus ring; it appears once you press a key.

askNoSideways.text: A long question no longer makes the Ask chat scroll sideways.

askScrollsDown.text: The Ask chat scrolls down to each new question.

importBookmarks.title: Import your browser bookmarks
importBookmarks.text: Bring in the bookmarks file from Chrome, Safari, Firefox or Edge. Keep its folders, put everything in one, or let AI sort the links by topic and review the groups first. Undo any import for 7 days. Import and export now live in Data & help in the sidebar.
importBookmarks.alt: The import dialog with two groups AI suggested for six links, one of them an existing folder.

newView.title: Build a view by hand or in words
newView.text: Save this view opens one dialog: set where, type, tags, words and sort, and watch the count. With AI on, describe it, like “Angular videos, newest first”, and AI fills the rows for you to check.
newView.alt: The new view dialog filled from the phrase “Angular videos, newest first”, with the matching link.

linkKinds.title: Ten kinds of links
linkKinds.text: Podcasts, documents, code, apps, posts and recipes join videos, articles and shopping. Shelfmark tells the kind when you save, and you can pick it in a view or in Edit link.
